prompt: A printable US Letter portrait page (8.5 by 11 inches) for a kids' pretend-play game, drawn flat and straight-on and filling the whole image: the page itself, not a photo or mockup of paper. Plain white paper with a clean white margin of about half an inch on every side where nothing is drawn, so it prints on a home printer. The game is "Cozy Café". Art style for the whole kit: bright, friendly flat vector cartoon like a modern kids' picture-book app: bold clean dark purple outlines, flat cheerful fills in coral red, sunny yellow, lime green, sky blue, deep purple and cream, soft rounded shapes, no gradients, no shading texture, no photo effects, lots of white paper. Ink-friendly: color sits on white, no full-page dark background. Draw a sheet of exactly 3 lanyard name badges, laid out 3 badges in one row across the top half, or 2 on top and 1 centered below, all the same size: tall rounded-rectangle tags with a punched hole and a little clip at the top center, a themed decorative border, one character picture in the upper half, the role title under it on a ribbon banner, and at the bottom the word "Name:" followed by a long blank line to write on. In order: badge 1: a cute cartoon character as the chef (tall white chef hat, holding a wooden spoon), title "Chef"; badge 2: a cute cartoon character as the waiter (bow tie, holding a notepad and a tray), title "Waiter"; badge 3: a cute cartoon character as the customer (napkin tucked in, holding a fork, smiling), title "Customer". The ONLY words on the page, spelled exactly letter for letter: "Chef", "Waiter", "Customer", "Name:". "Name:" appears once on every badge (3 times). Big, clear, rounded print letters, easy for a 5-year-old to read, dark on a light background, never curved along a path, never tiny. No other words, letters, numbers or signatures anywhere. Every badge identical in shape and size so they look like a set. Thin gray dashed cut lines around each piece, with wide white gutters between pieces so scissors fit. Kid-friendly and gentle, for ages 4 to 8: no guns, no knives, no real weapons (a toy sword is fine), no blood, nothing scary, no real people, no brands, no logos.
